title: Surprise and Shine Apple iPhone event live blog: Latest updates
content:
Macworld





Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event might be the most anticipated iPhone keynote in 10 years. It all kicks off tomorrow morning, and like you, we can’t wait. So join us as we count down the hours and minutes to the big show with all the latest rumors, leaks, and speculation leading up to the big event on Wednesday morning at 10 am PT.
Surprise and Shine iPhone event: How to watch
You can watch the full keynote right here using the embedded YouTube link below or on Apple.com on your iPhone or Mac. The “Watch Now” tab in the TV app on the Apple TV will also show the stream live.






Surprise and Shine iPhone event: What we expect
Apple might have dubbed this the “Surprise” event, but we have a pretty good idea what Apple is going to announce Wednesday morning. Here’s what we expect to see:
iPhone Ultra: Apple is almost certain to launch its first folding phone this week. We’re expecting a passport-style design with a 5.5-inch cover display and a near-8-inch inner display when opened.
iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max: We expect a similar design with a faster chip and a better camera system, possibly including a variable-aperture lens for the first time.
Apple Watch Series 12: The latest Apple Watch update will reportedly be a minor refresh with a new chip, all-day heart-rate tracking, and maybe the return of a ceramic finish.
Apple Watch Ultra 4: Like the Series 12, the Ultra 4 is expected to be a minor refresh largely focused on a new chip tuned for Siri AI.
AirPods 5: Apple is rumored to be launching a new pair of low-end AirPods, but we don’t know much about them.
Smart home: It’s less likely that Apple’s rumored smart-home hub arrives at this event, but we could see an updated Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini.
Surprise and Shine iPhone event: Live blog

This doesn’t necessarily confirm anything about the new phones other than the company thinks the rumors are pretty solid, since the design and colors they show almost perfectly match the reports we’ve been reading for months.

13 hours ago, By David Price
One More Thing… but what?
“We have great respect for these words,” said Tim Cook in 2017, “and we don’t use them lightly.” Those words, of course, were One More Thing.
That little phrase has signalled the arrival of some of Apple’s most iconic products and services, including the iMac G4, the MacBook Pro, FaceTime, the Apple Watch, Apple Music, and the iPhone X. Will it be uttered this year, and if so, what will it herald?
We discussed this on the podcast, and figured it would be a nice moment if new CEO John Ternus got the chance to utter those immortal words as part of his debut. (Debut as overall event host, that is. He’s spoken in individual segments before now.) The most obvious product to get the One More Thing treatment is the iPhone Ultra, but a bigger surprise would be the arrival of Apple’s long-rumored smart home hub. Either would work.
But Macworld readers put forward other ideas. At the less serious end, jimrock reckoned “It’d be really sick if he announced a $2,000 monitor stand” while Adam Moran proposed “One more thing: Now shipping iPhones with a charger.” Hashtag courage.
Moving on to things that could happen (but won’t), Rob K put forward “One more thing: iPhone Air 2 with 6,000 mAh silicon carbon battery, three cameras, and no stupid fold.” And Tower Lord suggested “AI-driven smart glasses. Minus the creep factor found in Meta glasses. Instead, true spatial computing. The ultimate personal computer.” Get rid of the AI part and we’re on board.
And finally, a note of sanity from Mike: “One more thing was Steve’s thing. Can we please stop measuring every CEO against Steve and let them be their own leaders?”
The last guy to say those three little words.

14 hours ago, By Michael Simon
All eyes on the crease
When Apple (allegedly) unveils its first folding iPhone tomorrow, Greg Joswiak or whomever gets the honor of announcing the phone on the stream, will talk about the displays, interface, cameras, design, and anything else Apple feels is worth highlighting. What they probably won’t spend a lot of time talking about is the crease.
Ever since Samsung’s first folding phone arrived, the center display crease has been an issue. It’s gotten better over the years, but it’s still the biggest hurdle for new customers to overcome. Even on the newest phones, you can see it when it’s opened and feel a little valley while using it. It’s flies in the face of Apple’s pursuit of perfection and likely the reason why we haven’t gotten a folding iPhone until now.
Earlier this year, it was reported that Apple had devised a way to overcome the crease with a combination of ultra-thin glass (UTG) and an optically clear adhesive that allows “the folding area to be locally thinned at the bending axis to improve bendability.” Samsung’s newest flagship phone features a display with a 60-micrometer UTG layer, which is likely a similar material to what Apple will use. 
No folding phone has been able to completely eliminate the crease. Will Apple be the first?

Luke Baker

iPhone Ultra, or iPhone Fold?
Sad to say for an event with the word surprise in its tagline, but there don’t seem to be many mysteries left concerning the foldable iPhone. With one notable exception: its name.
In the early days, most pundits referred to the rumored device as the iPhone Fold for obvious, logical reasons. But in the spring, we all started calling it the iPhone Ultra, even though, features-wise, that doesn’t entirely make sense. And with just one day to go until the announcement, case makers still can’t decide between the two options, with some plumping for Fold and others for Ultra in their pre-launch marketing materials.
And this all assumes that Apple won’t pull a last-minute switcheroo and go for iPhone Duo or iPhone Folio instead.
Over on our sister site Tech Advisor, Emma Rowley discusses the thorny question of the foldable iPhone’s name.

18 hours ago, By David Price
Will you fold?
Last year, the iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPhone Air competed for the title of Apple’s flagship handset. The Air was certainly more interesting, but the Pro Max was a far better specced, more powerful phone (not to mention more expensive). But this year there will only be one clear winner: the iPhone Ultra. Will you yield to temptation and pay what’s likely to be more than $2,000 for Apple’s first foldable smartphone?
One commenter on our YouTube channel is leaning towards no.
“If I was purchasing an iPhone and an iPad at the same time, then I would consider the Fold as it might work out cheaper than buying two separate devices,” writes christopherclarke6184. “But I am happy with my iPad M4 and iPhone 17 Pro Max so won’t be upgrading for a while… unless Apple has something special I may need. I’ll still be watching the show, though.”
Apple will be hoping for strong interest from the early adopter crowd, but given that this is an entirely new market for the company and a very high price, moderate sales may be enough in the short term.

Who is John Ternus?
One big difference this year is that the main host will be Apple’s new CEO, John Ternus, rather than Tim Cook. Ternus is a relative unknown to members of the public, and Apple fans will be keen to see how he handles hosting duties. Will he be a showman, like Steve Jobs? Quietly professional, like Cook? Or something new and unique to himself?
That’s not to say we’ve got no idea how he’ll carry himself in a presentation. As head of hardware Ternus spoke at multiple keynotes and product launches in the past, including the iPhone reveal last fall. His manner was very positive, with lots of superlatives, while being unafraid to delve into technical detail. But acting as main host is a different assignment, so we may see a new side to him on Wednesday.
In the meantime, read Alex Blake’s piece on the new boss, in which he describes Ternus as “the perfect CEO for this Apple era.”
John Ternus: A man with a passion for hardware.

1 day ago, By David Price
Surprise? What surprise?
Apple has given this week’s showcase the tagline “Surprise and Shine.” But what’s the big surprise? Apple’s September events are among its most predictable, almost always revolving around new iPhones and new Apple Watches, and sometimes new AirPods.
September 2025: iPhones, Apple Watches, AirPods
September 2024: iPhones, Apple Watches, AirPods
September 2023: iPhones, Apple Watches
September 2022: iPhones, Apple Watches, AirPods
September 2021: iPhones, Apple Watches, iPads
Is John Ternus going to spring a surprise in 2026? After asking this question on TikTok we’re unconvinced by the idea of an Apple alarm clock (sorry), but another reader’s proposal of a “tabletop Pixar light robot personal assistant with Siri” is a little more plausible. That sounds a lot like the rumored smart-home hub which Apple has been working on for years, and could make an appearance this week. It could even turn up as One More Thing at the end and make for a fun encore.
But ultimately the most likely outcome is that, as far as Apple is concerned, the widely expected foldable iPhone counts as the surprise. To those of us who live in the Apple rumor bubble the iPhone Ultra (or iPhone Fold) now looks like virtually a sure thing for Wednesday’s presentation, but to the wider community it’s far less well known. And officially, of course, it doesn’t even exist. Surprise!

Partly this allows the company to prune the colors which sold poorly the year before and experiment with alternatives, but the main advantage is that it allows customers to show off the fact they’ve got a new phone, even if the design is otherwise the same. The two new finishes are a little less garish: a dark-red/burgundy wine color, expected to be branded as Dark Cherry, and a light blue. Macworld exclusively revealed these colors in the summer.

title: The Apple Watch SE 3 is unavailable everywhere for some reason
content:
Macworld





In less the 24 hours, Apple will kick off its Surprise and Shine event and unveil its latest slate of new devices, including at least two new Apple Watches, the Series 12 and Ultra 4. But some pre-event shuffling at the Apple Store could point to a third watch announcement during the keynote.
Based on the rumors and its usual cadence, we expected the Apple Watch SE 3 to stick around for another 12 months. But on Monday afternoon, all models and colors suddenly disappeared from the online Apple Store. Whichever case, size, connectivity, or band you pick shows “Currently Unavailable” for shipping or pickup. Even on third-party resellers such as Amazon, the Apple Watch Series 3 doesn’t list a delivery date.
You can purchase an Apple Watch Series 11 or Ultra 3 without a problem.
It’s unclear what this means. Apple doesn’t typically stop selling old models ahead of announcements, instead opting to upgrade buyers to the latest model for devices that haven’t shipped. This could mean Apple plans to discontinue the line or change it significantly, requiring an immediate halt to sales.
We should find out what’s going on with the Apple Watch SE 3 after tomorrow’s keynote, which begins at 10 a.m. PT.

title: New product identifiers show up in Apple's backend, don't indicate release timing
content:
Apple is set to reveal a range of new products during its "Surprise and Shine" event on Wednesday, but a new set of product identifiers likely aren't indicative of what's being announced.


Device identifiers don't say anything about a product or when it will release
Product identifiers tell you very little about a product and often leave you guessing until they're found in official documentation for an already-released product. A list found in Apple's backend shows 37 new hardware identifiers for iPhones, Macs, and other products, but nothing else.
According to the social media post from code sleuth Aaron Perris, these new identifiers appeared in Apple's backend. While most are likely previously rumored products, at least one is a mystery.

title: UK repeats demands for child safety features that Apple already made
content:
Apple's child safety toolset is already robust and expanding with iOS 27, but the UK government isn't happy and continues to threaten legislation.


Apple already offers tools and APIs for protecting children from content they shouldn't be viewing or sending
Apple introduced Sensitive Content Warnings with iOS 17 in 2023 for child accounts and later introduced it as an option for adults. Several new features have been added since, including age verification systems in the UK, plus a comprehensive rethink of child safety with iOS 27 coming soon.
However, according to a report from Bloomberg, these measures aren't enough and legislation may still be necessary. UK Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has told the House of Commons that the government would introduce legislation on the matter, but didn't say when or to what extent.

title: Apple Likely to Announce Beats 360 This Month
content:
Apple today released a firmware update (4A203) for its upcoming Beats 360 headphones, suggesting that a launch is approaching. With the firmware now available, it seems likely that Apple will announce the Beats 360 at some point in September.


Beats 360 have already leaked across multiple regulatory databases and retail listings over the past several months, and soccer stars like Lamine Yamal and Antonee Robinson were spotted wearing them around the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

MacRumors was first to report on the Beats 360 name last month after the headphones appeared in various retail listings on Amazon and other reseller websites, some of which have since been removed. The listings revealed that the headphones will be available in Black, Cloud, Sky, and Pink, at a minimum. There will also be interchangeable Performance Knit and UltraPlush ear cushions and headbands that come in those same four colors, plus extra options like Volt and Navy, allowing you to create your own personalized look.

Beats Studio Pro that came out in 2023.


The listing also said that the Beats 360 are Apple's first-ever sweat-resistant and water-resistant over-ear headphones, with an IPX4 rating.

MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris, the Beats 360 will support hands-free Siri, meaning that you can say "Hey Siri" or simply "Siri" to activate the assistant.

Beats 360 will come with a set of interchangeable Performance Knit cushions and a woven ripstop fabric carrying case, but customers will need to supply their own USB-C charging cable and power adapter. One listing said the headphones will be priced at $299.99 in the U.S., but we cannot confirm if that information is accurate.

Beats Studio Pro are regularly priced at $349.99.

title: iOS 26.6.2 is out now to fix a cellular update bug
content:
Macworld





We expect Apple to release iOS 27 next week ahead of the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro, but before that happens, there’s one last update to iOS 26. The iOS 26.6.2 update (also iPadOS 26.6.2) fixes one minor but important bug. The release notes are as follows:
This update fixes an issue that prevents downloading a software update over a cellular connection.
It looks like that’s all there is in this update. There is no associated macOS release (it would be macOS 26.6.3), and the Apple security releases page lists no new fixes associated with this release.
To update your iPhone, head over to Settings, then General and Software Update, and follow the prompts.

title: How to Watch Apple's 'Surprise and Shine' September 9 Event
content:
Apple is hosting an online streaming event for the public and press on Wednesday, September 9 at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time. The company is expected to announce new iPhone 18 Pro models and a new foldable iPhone alongside new Apple Watch models, and potentially AirPods 5 and other products during the event, dubbed "Sunshine and Shine." Here's how you can watch it and when, wherever you are in the world.


There are multiple ways to watch the September 9 event, with details listed below. We've also included a useful guide on when the event will take place in your particular time zone.

Apple Events Website

With the Apple Events website, you can watch the event live on a Mac, iPhone, ‌iPad‌, PC, or any other device with a web browser. The Apple Events website works in Safari, Chrome, Firefox, and other main browsers.

 
www.apple.com/apple-events/ using a web browser at the appropriate time to watch. You can visit the site now to add an event reminder to your calendar.

YouTube

Apple also plans to stream the event live on YouTube, which is perhaps the easiest and most efficient way to watch because the YouTube live stream can be viewed on every platform where YouTube is available, which is pretty much all platforms, from smartphones and tablets to consoles and smart TVs.



Apple has posted a placeholder for the September 9 event on YouTube, and you can visit it now to set an event reminder.

Apple TV App

Apple used to have a dedicated Apple Events app on the Apple TV, but ahead of WWDC 2020, it was folded into the Apple TV app. On event day, there will be a prominent ‌Apple TV‌ app section dedicated to the live stream, which can be watched on any device where the ‌Apple TV‌ app is available.

If you have an ‌Apple TV‌, the ‌Apple TV‌ app is one of the best ways to watch the event live. Apple hasn't updated the ‌Apple TV‌ app with the new event as of yet, but it should be added soon.

title: Potential iPhone 18 Pro camera software features found in iOS 27 beta code
content:
Macworld





The iPhone 18 Pro is almost here. On the eve of Apple’s big Surprise and Shine event, we have some last-minute info on what we might expect from the camera on Apple’s new Pro iPhone.
This latest leak comes via MacRumors, where one of its regular forum members found some code in the iOS 27 beta that points to five potential new Camera software features:
Exposure scopes: Adds waveforms or histograms for the viewfinder to better see exposure across your shot.
Focus peaking and highlight warnings: Another common professional camera feature, focus peaking highlights edges that are in focus, and highlight warnings mark areas of the viewfinder (usually with zebra-stripes) that are overexposed and will be blown out.
Repeated self-timer shots: Lets you take several shots in a row, with a countdown timer in between.
Manual focus: A control to set and lock focus, similar to what is found in the Final Cut Camera app. There was something like this in iOS 26, but the first iOS 27 beta removed it. MacRumors says the underlying focus-locking code is still there, but Apple has restricted it to devices that ship with ‌iOS 27‌ or later.
Aperture-based image correction: This is a change to the image processing pipeline to account for variable apertures on the same camera. A variable-aperture wide camera is one of the expected features of the iPhone 18 Pro Max and possibly the regular iPhone 18 Pro as well.
Only that last feature—which is more of an internal processing change—would rely on the new camera hardware in the iPhone 18 Pro, which has been rumored. The rest could easily come to all modern iPhone cameras, and in fact those exact features have been found in third-party camera apps for years (and the Manual Focus in Apple’s own apps). Still, Apple sometimes locks software features to new devices even when not strictly necessary as a way to make a new hardware purchase more appealing.
We’ll find out more on September 9 at Apple’s Surprise and Shine event.

title: Apple Event Tomorrow: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra Cheat Sheet
content:
Apple's biggest event of the year is almost here, and all eyes are on Cupertino. With the first foldable iPhone expected to headline Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event on Wednesday, September 9, at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time, the rumor mill has been running full throttle, fuelled by the biggest single design change in the life of the iPhone.



To get you up to speed, here's a quick reference guide to the rumoured upgrades, expected prices, and possible pre-order/release dates of everything we're expecting to see tomorrow.

Rumors by Model

iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max


Similar overall design to the iPhone 17 Pro models, with a more uniform finish across the aluminum and glass back.

  
Smaller Dynamic Island, said to be achieved by Apple moving some Face ID components beneath the screen.

  
More efficient LTPO+ displays.

  
A20 Pro chip manufactured using TSMC's 2nm process.

  
12GB of RAM and 256GB starting storage.

  
Variable-aperture main camera for greater control over light and background blur – although reports disagree on whether this will be exclusive to the Pro Max.

  
Possible Samsung image sensor for improved image quality and camera responsiveness.

  
Simplified Camera Control button that retains pressure sensing but removes the capacitive layer.

  
Larger battery in the Pro Max, which could well result in a slightly thicker and heavier body.

  
Possible Apple C2 modem, although U.S. models could retain Qualcomm modems for mmWave support.

  
The strongest color rumors include Dark Cherry, Light Blue, and Silver. Other rumors have suggested no Silver, and a black finish has also been suggested.


iPhone Ultra (Foldable)


Apple's first folding iPhone, with "iPhone Ultra" among the rumored names, with "iPhone Fold" and "iPhone Duo" remaining outlying possibilities.

  
Book-style design with an approximately 5.5-inch outer display and 7.8-inch inner display.

  
Chassis measuring just 4.5mm thick when unfolded.

  
Liquid-metal hinge and an extremely inconspicuous – but not completely invisible – display crease.

  
Touch ID integrated into the Side button in lieu of Face ID.

  
Wide and Ultra Wide rear cameras, plus selfie cameras on both the outer and inner displays.

  
A20 Pro chip and an expected 12GB of RAM.

  
MagSafe charging support.

  
iPad-like multitasking, including side-by-side apps.

  
Silver/white and a very dark indigo finish among the rumored colors.


Apple Watch Series 12


Familiar design, with no major change to the case expected.

  
Faster S12 chip and improvements to health and fitness tracking.

  
Possible return of a ceramic case, with white and dark gray versions reportedly tested.

  
Continuous heart-rate monitoring throughout the day among the features Apple is testing, along with a new "Readiness" app.

  
More wellness metrics through revamped Health and Fitness experiences.


Apple Watch Ultra 4


Similar design to the Apple Watch Ultra 3.

  
Faster S12 chip and related health and fitness improvements.

  
Likely continuous heart-rate collection if the Series 12 gets it.

  
Possible expansion of satellite capabilities, including Apple Maps and photo sharing in Messages.


AirPods 5 (Possible)


Two versions expected, with and without active noise cancellation.

  
Possible H3 chip for better sound quality and lower latency.


iPhone 18 (Regular)

The regular iPhone 18 is not expected to feature tomorrow. Apple is reportedly moving that model's launch to spring 2027, when the iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2 are also expected to debut as part of a new split-year release schedule.

iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra Pricing Expectations

Higher memory costs could push up prices for both Pro models this year. Based on TrendForce's forecasts for the Pro models and Bloomberg's latest reporting on the foldable, the possible U.S. starting prices are:

  

    Model
Estimated Starting Price

  

    iPhone 18 Pro
$1,249–$1,299

  

    iPhone 18 Pro Max
$1,349–$1,399

  

    iPhone Ultra
$2,199 (rumored)



Bloomberg's Mark Gurman today also reported that Apple has discussed a $2,199 starting price for the foldable, with some upgraded storage configurations potentially approaching $3,000. Reliable figures for every storage tier are not available. 

When Can I Pre-order iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra?

iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders could begin on Saturday, September 12, at midnight Pacific Time / 3 a.m. Eastern Time. The potential Saturday opening would avoid September 11, similar to Apple's approach in 2015.

manufacturing challenges potentially delaying a release until the fourth quarter of 2026. However, Gurman has said he would be "very surprised" if the foldable iPhone does not come out at the same time as the iPhone 18 Pro models or "very close" to them. 

When Do iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra Launch?

Friday, September 18 is the most likely release date for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. It's our best educated guess, but we believe that is when deliveries and retail availability will begin. 

As already mentioned, reports remain divided on the foldable's launch schedule. There's still a possibility that its unveiling tomorrow may precede its arrival in stores by several weeks or more.

Follow MacRumors.com and our MacRumorsLive account on Twitter (X) for coverage as the announcements happen. We'll have individual stories on the new products, followed by more detailed looks at their features, pricing, and availability throughout the week. Stay tuned!

title: Code leak reveals four new Apple Watch Series 12 features
content:
Macworld





The headline announcements of tomorrow’s Surprise and Shine press event will revolve around the iPhone, but don’t forget the Apple Watch. We’re expecting some quietly valuable updates to the market-leading smartwatch, and a new code leak offers hints about what exactly Apple is about to reveal.
According to pdfu, a regular contributor to the MacRumors forums, the new models (the Series 12 and Ultra 4) will get four upgrades on the previous generation. This prediction is based on insights gleaned from watchOS 27 and iOS 27 beta code. Here are the highlights from what they’ve found:
1. A new optical sensor
watchOS 27 mentions a new optical sensing family called Sunstone4p0, which suggests the new watches will get a hardware upgrade in this area. According to pdfu’s findings, the new sensor seems likely to feature improved signal filtering and lower electronic noise for more accurate heart readings when the pulse signal is weak. It’s also been previously reported that the new watches will have continuous heart-rate tracking, which also somewhat corroborates the need for a new sensor.
2. Extra storage
A storage profile associated with T8320, widely believed to be the CPU of the Series 12 and Ultra 4, is labelled 1024gb. This suggests the new watches will have 1,024 gigabits, or 128GB, of storage, up from 64GB on current models. That’s a lot for a watch and probably means at least some Apple Intelligence stuff wil be stored on the device.
3. A new app
The Apple Watch is about to get a new pre-installed app called Readiness. This feels like something that would be included in the watchOS 27 announcements at WWDC in the summer, but it wasn’t: pdfu thinks Apple “may be holding back some of the biggest features in watchOS 27 for its September launch.”
It isn’t clear what Readiness will do, but the name and placement in the default app grid suggest something to do with preparing for or recovering from a workout. In a partial corroboration of this prediction, Mark Gurman says Readiness will be a variant of the Vitals app and “compete with software from Whoop & Oura.”
4. Better strength workouts
The Workout app is one of the Apple Watch’s greatest strengths. Ironically, however, strength workouts specifically are currently quite weak. You simply can’t record a lot of data about your weights sessions. As of this fall, and based on iOS 27 and watchOS 27 betas, that’s about to change. You’ll be able to record multiple sets, with varied weights and reps, as part of a single workout.
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are expected to be announced as part of the Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday, September 9. For all the latest news and rumors heading up to the event, check our regularly updated Apple Watch Series 12 superguide.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4: Release date & latest features before Apple’s event
content:
Macworld





Apple is expected to unveil the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 at its September 9 event, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and foldable iPhone Ultra. An Apple Watch SE 4 is not expected.
Don’t expect a major redesign. Both watches should look much like their predecessors, although Apple has reportedly tested white and dark gray ceramic finishes. A new, faster S-series chip is expected to be one of the main upgrades.
Health changes could include continuous heart-rate data collection, while other new sensors remain possible. However, blood-glucose monitoring still appears years away, and Touch ID now looks unlikely despite appearing in prototype code.
watchOS 27 will bring Siri AI, a redesigned Find My app and other software improvements. Pricing is less certain: the Series 12 could rise from $399 to around $429, while the Ultra 4 may stay close to $799. Read on for our roundup of all the rumors about the new Apple Watches for 2026. 


Which Apple Watches are expected on September 9?
Apple is expected to unveil two new Apple Watch models at its “Surprise and Shine” event on September 9: the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.
Apple Watch is one of the few Apple products that receives a predictable annual update, so a Series 12 launch is widely expected. The Ultra 4 is also due to replace the current Ultra 3.
Neither model is expected to receive a major redesign. Instead, both are likely to be relatively modest “chip and ship” updates, focusing on new processors, connectivity and other internal improvements while retaining broadly similar designs.
Which Apple Watch isn’t expected to be updated?
The Apple Watch SE 4 is not expected to launch in 2026. Apple updated its budget model with the Apple Watch SE 3 in 2025, and that version is likely to remain in the lineup for another year.


						

							


What new features are expected: At a glance
Apple Watch Series 12: expected new features
The Apple Watch Series 12 is expected to be a modest upgrade, led by a faster S-series chip and potentially a larger battery. The design should remain largely unchanged, though ceramic finishes are possible. Continuous heart-rate monitoring is reportedly in testing, while Touch ID looks unlikely. Siri AI and other watchOS 27 features should provide the biggest everyday changes.
Apple Watch Ultra 4: expected new features
The Apple Watch Ultra 4 should retain the Ultra 3’s rugged design while gaining the same new S-series chip. Satellite connectivity will remain a key advantage, with watchOS 27 expected to expand its capabilities. Continuous heart-rate monitoring and Siri AI are also possible, while a major redesign, Touch ID and blood-glucose monitoring appear unlikely.


						

							






FeatureApple Watch Series 12Apple Watch Ultra 4

LaunchExpected September 9, 2026Expected September 9, 2026
DesignNo major redesign expectedNo major redesign expected
New finishesCeramic reportedly tested; new colors possibleNew colors/finishes possible
ProcessorNew, faster S-series chip, likely S11 or S12Same new S-series chip expected
BatteryLarger battery reportedly being explored; potentially longer runtimeNo firm larger-battery rumor; efficiency improvements possible
Heart-rate monitoringContinuous data collection reportedly testedContinuous data collection reportedly tested
Blood-glucose monitoringUnlikely in 2026Unlikely in 2026
Touch IDTested internally, but now considered unlikelyUnlikely
5GContinues from current generationContinues from current generation
Satellite connectivityNo strong evidence of direct satellite supportExpected to retain satellite connectivity

Readiness appRumoredRumored
Expected priceAround $399–$429; $429 is speculativeLikely close to $799
Overall upgradeInternal, health and software refinementInternal, health, software and satellite refinement

 






What is the Apple Watch 2026 release date?
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are expected to be announced at Apple’s September iPhone event on Wednesday, September 9, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and the new iPhone Ultra.
Apple has launched a new Series Apple Watch every September since 2016, usually alongside the latest iPhones, so the arrival of the Series 12 is all but certain. The Ultra 4 is also widely expected to appear at the event.
Preorders are likely to open shortly after the announcement, with shipping expected to begin later in September.


						

							


Apple Watch 2026 chips
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are expected to feature a new, faster S-series chip, although there is some uncertainty over whether Apple will call it the S11 or S12.
Unlike some recent Apple Watch generations, where processor changes have been relatively modest, the 2026 chip is expected to deliver a more meaningful improvement in performance and efficiency. It should also provide more headroom for new watchOS 27 features and increasingly demanding on-device AI capabilities.
That could be particularly important as Apple raises the hardware requirements for watchOS. watchOS 27 supports Apple Watches with an S9 chip or later, dropping several older models, suggesting newer silicon is becoming increasingly important for features such as Apple’s more advanced Siri capabilities.
As a result, the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are widely expected to be relatively straightforward “chip and ship” updates, with the processor upgrade among the most significant changes. A faster chip could also help keep the new watches compatible with major watchOS features for longer.


						

							


Will the 2026 Apple Watch get a new design?

				
					

				
			Apple Watches have looked roughly the same for years.
David Price / Foundry




A major redesign is not expected for the 2026 Apple Watch lineup. Both the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are likely to retain the same overall design language as their predecessors, with this year’s upgrades focused more heavily on internal changes.
Last summer, a DigiTimes report raised hopes that 2026 could bring the Apple Watch its first substantial redesign in years. However, similar rumors have appeared before without materialising, including reports of a dramatically redesigned Apple Watch Series X.
More recently, Weibo leaker Instant Digital claimed that neither the Series 12 nor the Series 13 will receive a major new look, with a more significant redesign instead expected in 2028.
There has also been little evidence from Apple’s supply chain of a radically redesigned chassis. We’d therefore expect the Series 12 to retain the slimmer case and larger display of recent models, while the Ultra 4 should stick with its familiar rugged design. Smaller changes such as new colors, finishes, slightly slimmer bezels, or display tweaks remain possible.
One potentially more noticeable change could be the return of ceramic. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has reported that Apple has tested white and dark gray ceramic Apple Watch models, which could bring back a premium material Apple last offered with the Apple Watch Edition in 2019.
Will the Apple Watch get a new display?

				
					

				
			The Series 11 has an always-on screen, but it leaves something to be desired on the brightness front.
David Price / Foundry




A more substantial display upgrade is possible eventually, but it doesn’t look certain for 2026.
Apple has used OLED displays since the original Apple Watch, with recent Series models reaching up to 2,000 nits of brightness and the Ultra 3 reaching 3,000 nits. For several years there have been reports that Apple wants to move to microLED, which could offer better color accuracy, greater efficiency, and significantly higher brightness.
At CES 2025, Samsung demonstrated a microLED smartwatch display capable of 4,000 nits, showing the potential of the technology. However, while microLED remains a plausible future Apple Watch upgrade, there is currently little evidence that it will arrive with the Series 12 or Ultra 4 in 2026.


						

							


Will the Apple Watch Series 12 have longer battery life?

				
					

				
			
Petter Ahrnstedt




There are signs that battery life could be a bigger focus for the Apple Watch Series 12, although any improvement has yet to be confirmed.
According to Weibo leaker Instant Digital, Apple is prioritising battery capacity and health sensors, and is reportedly trying to fit a physically larger battery inside the Series 12 rather than relying solely on efficiency gains from the new processor.
That could help Apple extend battery life beyond the 24 hours of normal use offered by the Apple Watch Series 11. Even a modest increase would be useful for sleep tracking and other always-on health features, which leave less time for charging.
So while a dramatic leap in battery life isn’t guaranteed, the Series 12 could combine a larger battery with efficiency improvements from its new chip to deliver longer real-world runtime.
Will the Apple Watch Ultra get a better battery?
The rumor about a larger battery currently applies specifically to the Series 12, rather than the Ultra 4. The Ultra already offers substantially longer battery life, with Apple rating the Ultra 3 for up to 42 hours of normal use and up to 72 hours in Low Power Mode.


						

							


What connectivity changes are coming with the 2026 Apple Watches?
Major connectivity changes are not currently expected for the 2026 Apple Watch lineup.
5G is already supported on current cellular Apple Watch models and there are also no strong reports pointing to a major new cellular modem upgrade this year.
However, Satellite connectivity is more significant, but it is primarily an Apple Watch Ultra feature. The current Ultra 3 already supports Emergency SOS, Find My, and Messages via satellite, and the Ultra 4 is expected to retain those capabilities.
watchOS 27 is also expected to expand what Apple Watch can do over satellite, with features including Apple Maps via satellite and the ability to send and receive photos in Messages via satellite. Those software features should be available on the Ultra 4 where supported.
There is currently no evidence that the Apple Watch Series 12 will gain direct satellite connectivity, so this is likely to remain one of the key differences between the standard Series model and the Ultra.


						

							


Will Apple Watch Series 12 get Touch ID?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Probably not in 2026.
Macworld uncovered developer code referring to the 2026 Apple Watch models alongside “AppleMesa,” Apple’s internal codename for Touch ID. No previous Apple Watch models had included similar references, suggesting Apple has at least tested fingerprint authentication for the Watch.
At the time, that raised the possibility that Touch ID could debut with the Series 12, potentially built into a side button or beneath the display. It would be useful for Apple Pay, private apps and messages, and unlocking the Watch independently of an iPhone.
However, more recent reporting has made a 2026 launch look much less likely. One leaker has claimed Apple is not bringing Touch ID to the Apple Watch, while other reports suggest Apple is prioritising larger batteries and new health sensors over using valuable internal space for fingerprint hardware.
The earlier code may therefore relate to prototype hardware rather than a feature destined for this year’s models.
For now, Touch ID appears to be something Apple has explored for the Watch, but it is unlikely to debut with the Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4. 
Apple Watch already uses passcode and wrist-detection security, and it can also act as an authenticator for other Apple devices, including automatically unlocking a Mac.


						

							


What health features are coming to the 2026 Apple Watches?
Health and fitness tracking is expected to remain a major focus for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. The most credible new feature is continuous heart-rate monitoring throughout the day, while Apple may also make further improvements to its existing health sensors and hypertension features.
More ambitious additions, including non-invasive blood-glucose monitoring and AI-powered health coaching, remain in development but are much less likely to arrive this year.
Continuous heart-rate monitoring
One of the most significant rumored upgrades for the Series 12 and Ultra 4 is continuous heart-rate data collection.
According to a report in August from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has tested technology that would allow the Apple Watch heart-rate sensor to “continuously collect data throughout the day.”
Currently, Apple Watch takes periodic background heart-rate readings when you aren’t using the Workout, Mindfulness, or Heart Rate apps. Continuous monitoring could provide a much richer dataset, potentially improving health trends, alerts, and other analysis.
Will Apple Watch Series 12 monitor blood glucose?
Apple has been working on non-invasive blood-glucose monitoring for many years, but it remains unlikely to arrive with the Series 12.
Reports of Apple’s work on the technology date back to at least 2017, when we reported that the company had assembled a team of biomedical engineers to investigate continuous glucose monitoring.
Bloomberg subsequently reported that Apple had developed a system based on optical absorption spectroscopy and had reached the proof-of-concept stage. However, more recent reporting suggests a commercial Apple Watch implementation may still be several years away, potentially around 2030.
So while blood-glucose monitoring remains one of Apple Watch’s most anticipated future features, Series 12 is probably too soon.
What about AI health coaching?

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple has also been developing an AI-powered health and fitness coaching system, previously reported under the name Health+.
The project has reportedly been scaled back from a single ambitious service into individual features that can be released progressively. That means some AI-powered health insights or coaching features could appear sooner, but there is currently little evidence that a complete Health+ service will debut with the Series 12.
For 2026, continuous heart-rate monitoring looks considerably more plausible than either blood-glucose monitoring or a full AI health coach.
What health features does Apple Watch already have?
The Series 11 and Ultra 3 already offer an extensive set of health features, including:
Blood Oxygen monitoring
ECG
Heart-rate and heart-rhythm notifications
Hypertension notifications
Wrist-temperature sensing
Cycle Tracking and ovulation estimates
Sleep stages and Sleep Score
Sleep apnea notifications
The Apple Watch SE 3 has a more limited health feature set and lacks Blood Oxygen monitoring, ECG, temperature sensing, and hypertension notifications.


						

							


What new apps are coming to Apple Watch?






watchOS 27 will bring several new apps and app experiences to the Apple Watch, although Apple appears to be focusing as much on upgrading existing software as adding entirely new apps and some older Apple Watches will not be able to run watchOS 27. 
Siri AI comes to Apple Watch
The biggest software addition is Siri AI. Apple Watch users will be able to start Siri AI conversations from their wrist, access previous conversations across Apple devices, and use newer capabilities such as personal context and web answers.
Much of the processing will still depend on a nearby compatible iPhone, but the change should make Apple Watch a much more useful entry point for Apple’s AI features.
watchOS 27 with Siri AI requires an Apple Watch Series 9 or later, Ultra 2 or later, or SE 3, alongside a compatible iPhone.
Find My gets a major overhaul
Apple is also introducing a unified Find My app, replacing the separate Find People, Find Devices and Find Items apps with a single map-based interface.
That should make it much easier to locate people, Apple devices and AirTags directly from the Watch without jumping between multiple apps.
A new Readiness app could be coming
Late-breaking code discovered in September reportedly points to a separate Readiness app for Apple Watch.
The app is thought to focus on recovery and preparedness, potentially using health and fitness data to indicate how ready you are for exercise or other activity. However, this has not yet been officially announced, so it should still be treated as a rumor.
Existing apps are getting smarter too
Apple is also improving several existing Watch apps and features rather than simply adding new ones.
Workout Buddy is becoming more capable, with smarter fitness insights, Spanish-language support and the ability to work without a direct iPhone connection. Wallet gains the ability to display card balances, while the Smart Stack adds new interactions, including a tap gesture for selecting widgets.
watchOS 27 also introduces a more dynamic app grid that surfaces five contextually relevant apps, while Apple continues to make its Watch apps look and behave more like their iPhone equivalents.
Overall, the most important software additions for 2026 are Siri AI, the redesigned Find My app and the possible new Readiness app, with broader improvements across Workout, Wallet and the Smart Stack.
watchOS 27 also expands women’s health features with pre-menopause tracking.


						

							


How much could the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 cost?
Apple has not announced pricing for the 2026 Apple Watch lineup but we can make some estimations especially in the light of Apple’s dramatic price rises for iPads and Macs in June 2026. 
The current Apple Watch Series 11 starts at $399, while the Apple Watch Ultra 3 starts at $799. Apple left Watch pricing unchanged when it raised prices across much of its Mac, iPad and home-device lineup in June 2026, which suggests the new models could still avoid a major increase.
However, Apple warned at the time that further price rises could follow, and some analysts expect higher component costs to result in a modest increase for the next Apple Watch generation.
Apple Watch Series 12 price prediction
We think the Series 12 could start at around $429, up from $399 for the Series 11, although this is a prediction rather than a firm rumor. A smaller increase — or no increase at all — remains possible.
The cellular version currently starts at $499 and would likely rise by a similar amount if Apple increases prices across the range.
Apple Watch Ultra 4 price prediction
There are fewer specific pricing rumors surrounding the Ultra 4, so the safest assumption is that it will remain close to the Ultra 3’s $799 starting price.
Apple could apply a modest increase here too, but there is currently little evidence pointing to a substantial Ultra price rise.
What about the Apple Watch SE?
An Apple Watch SE 4 is not expected in 2026, so the SE 3 should remain Apple’s entry-level model at or near its current $249 starting price.


						

							


Does it matter if these are only incremental updates?
Not necessarily. The Apple Watch is now a mature product, so Apple’s focus has increasingly shifted from major redesigns to smaller improvements in performance, battery life, connectivity, durability, and health features.
As we argued in July 2026, the Apple Watch doesn’t necessarily need another dramatic redesign or a flashy new feature. What matters more at this stage is a steady stream of quality-of-life improvements that make it more useful day to day.
That was also true of the previous generation. The Series 11 added 5G connectivity, better battery life and improved durability, while the Ultra 3 brought a slightly larger display and satellite connectivity. Neither was a radical reinvention, but both refined an already well-established design.
The Apple Watch’s overall look has changed relatively little since the Series 4 redesign in 2018, and that may be deliberate. For existing owners of a recent model, the Series 12 and Ultra 4 may not offer a compelling reason to upgrade. But for anyone coming from an older Apple Watch, several generations of incremental improvements can add up to a much more substantial upgrade.


						

							


Is Apple considering a circular Apple Watch design?
Yes — but that doesn’t mean one is likely to go on sale.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in August 2026 that Apple has explored several new wearable concepts, including circular displays similar to those used by the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch. Apple is also reportedly considering other ideas, such as screenless fitness trackers, as it looks for ways to reinvent its wearable lineup.
However, these concepts appear to be experimental and are not expected to arrive soon.
A circular Apple Watch would also involve significant compromises. The current rectangular design makes efficient use of screen space for text, apps and complications, while a round display would reduce usable area at the same overall width. That could also leave less internal room for components such as the battery and health sensors.
For those reasons, a round Apple Watch is best viewed as something Apple has explored rather than a likely future product.


						

							


Will Apple ever redesign the Apple Watch?
Almost certainly, but a major redesign may still be some way off.
Apple is reportedly experimenting with different form factors as competition in wearables grows, and Gurman has said the company is “determined to reinvent the lineup.” But the more radical ideas currently under consideration — including circular displays and screenless wearables — are said to be longer-term projects.
For now, Apple appears more likely to continue refining the existing rectangular Apple Watch design before making a more fundamental change.

title: Apple Sued Over Alleged Face ID Patent Infringement
content:
TrinamiX, a subsidiary of the German chemical giant BASF, is suing Apple in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas, accusing the company of infringing seven patents related to face authentication technology used in Face ID.


In its complaint, first reported by Reuters, trinamiX said it spent years developing technology to stop people from fooling face unlock systems with a photo, a fake mask, or a silicone copy of someone's face.

The complaint says Apple's original version of ‌Face ID‌, introduced with the iPhone X in 2017, did not use trinamiX's technology, but that newer iPhones and iPads do. TrinamiX's system is designed to tell real skin apart from things like photos or masks, essentially adding a check that catches fakes conventional optical face scanning methods would miss.

The complaint alleges that "Apple knew or should have known of the high probability that updating its iPhones and iPads to incorporate ‌Face ID‌ using material and skin detection" infringed seven trinamiX patents, causing "substantial damages and irreparable injury." The seven patents cover two areas: detecting skin during face unlock and identifying what material something is made of.

iPhone 16, iPhone 16e, ‌iPhone 16‌ Plus, ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro, ‌iPhone 16‌ Pro Max, iPhone 17, iPhone 17e, iPhone 17 Pro, ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ Max, iPhone Air, 11-inch iPad Pro (4th generation), 12.9-inch ‌iPad Pro‌ (6th generation), and the 11- and 13-inch ‌iPad Pro‌ models with the M4 and M5 chips. 

IP Fray.

title: Foldable iPhone Development History and Price Revealed in New Report
content:
Former Apple CEO Tim Cook played a major role in the development of the foldable iPhone, which could reach around $3,000 with storage upgrades, according to new details shared by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. 


Early in the development of the foldable iPhone, the company reportedly targeted a starting retail price of $1,999, hoping to come under the "potentially controversial $2,000 barrier." The idea was to replicate the debut of the iPhone X in 2017, which started at $999.

Amid the impact of the global memory shortage, Apple is said to have recently discussed pricing the foldable at $2,199. Some storage configurations could approach $3,000. While the company anticipates some "sticker shock" for consumers, the willingness of customers to spend around $2,000 on iPhone models with upgraded storage convinced the company that an "upscale foldable device was worth bringing to market."

Gurman also revealed details about the history of the foldable iPhone inside Apple. Around 2020, Cook apparently returned from a visit to Asia "unusually energized" about foldable phones. During the trip, he saw growing numbers of consumers using foldable devices from the likes of Samsung and Huawei. He came to believe that Apple needed an equivalent offering in the market and pushed the company to accelerate its development efforts. 

iPad mini that could unfold into a larger tablet. Cook wanted the final device to be more mainstream in the form of a foldable iPhone, and his level of involvement in the project was unusual. 

The project was conceived under Dan Riccio, who preceded John Ternus as head of hardware engineering. The company apparently prioritized resolving four main challenges: reducing the visibility of the display crease, improving hinge reliability, creating a new flexible cover glass for the inner display, and developing under-display camera technology. 

The company eventually settled on a hinge system made using titanium and aluminum and custom cover glass developed with Corning. Despite being less durable than other existing iPhone models, Apple is said to believe that the construction quality of the foldable iPhone is industry-leading for the foldable market, and thinks it has an advantage over Android devices in terms of software. 

Gurman restated several of the device's rumored specifications, including a 7.8-inch inner display, a 5.5-inch outer display, and a wide form-factor design. During development, Apple designers apparently compared the folded proportions of the device to a passport and the unfolded proportions to a Magic Trackpad. The short-and-wide design was chosen to provide a point of differentiation with rival foldable and generate  consumer interest.

He reiterated that the foldable iPhone may be less durable than a conventional iPhone, with an inferior camera system and less battery life. Despite these drawbacks, Apple employees are said to believe "the company will sell every foldable phone it can produce."

Gurman also noted that the foldable iPhone's engineering complexity "makes it an ideal showcase" for new CEO John Ternus, following his career as Apple's hardware chief. Ternus was apparently a major champion of the device and played a major role to "push it over the finish line," alongside Cook.

title: 2024 vs. 2026 Mac Mini Buyer's Guide
content:
Last month, Apple announced a new Mac mini built around the all-new M6 chip and the M5 Pro, replacing the M4 and M4 Pro models that had been on sale since October 2024. Pre-orders are open now, with the machines arriving to customers and in stores on September 22.


The M6 model starts at $899 and the M5 Pro model at $1,699, each $100 above what its predecessor was selling for by the end of its run and $300 above what their predecessors launched at. The ‌Mac mini‌ rose from $599 to $799 in May, and the M4 Pro configuration went from $1,399 to $1,599 in June, both as a consequence of the memory shortage driven by AI demand. Education pricing brings the new models down to $799 and $1,599 respectively.

What Changed Across Both Models

A number of upgrades apply equally to the standard and Pro configurations, regardless of which chip you choose:
 


‌Mac mini‌ (2024)
‌Mac mini‌ (2026)



Neural Accelerators in each GPU core



Variable refresh rate and HDR support


Wi-Fi 6E connectivity
Wi-Fi 7 connectivity



Apple N1 wireless networking chip


Bluetooth 5.3
Bluetooth 6



Thread networking technology


Gigabit Ethernet or 10Gb Ethernet
2.5Gb Ethernet or 10Gb Ethernet



Genlock support over USB-C




Mac Mini With M4 vs. M6

Here is everything else that differs between the M4 and M6 versions of the ‌Mac mini‌:
 


‌Mac mini‌ (M4)
‌Mac mini‌ (M6)


M4 chip
M6 chip


10-core CPU with four performance cores and six efficiency cores
12-core CPU with two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores


10-core GPU
12-core GPU


16-core Neural Engine
Dual 16-core Neural Engine


120GB/s memory bandwidth
153GB/s memory bandwidth, rising to 170GB/s with 24GB or 32GB of unified memory


Two displays up to 6K at 60Hz, plus a third up to 5K at 60Hz
Two displays up to 6K at 60Hz or 4K at 165Hz, plus a third up to 5K at 60Hz



Up to two external displays over a single Thunderbolt port


Now discontinued
From $899




Mac Mini With M4 Pro vs. M5 Pro

The comparison below outlines the remaining differences between the two Pro configurations:
 


‌Mac mini‌ (M4 Pro)
‌Mac mini‌ (M5 Pro)


M4 Pro chip
M5 Pro chip


Base: 12-core CPU with eight performance cores and four efficiency cores
Configurable to: 14-core CPU
Base: 15-core CPU with five super cores and 10 performance cores
Configurable to: 18-core CPU



Enhanced shader core and third-generation ray tracing


273GB/s memory bandwidth
307GB/s memory bandwidth


Three displays up to 6K at 60Hz
Three displays up to 6K at 60Hz or 4K at 165Hz


Two displays: one up to 8K at 60Hz or 4K at 240Hz, plus a second up to 6K at 60Hz
Two displays: one up to 8K at 60Hz, 5K at 120Hz, or 4K at 240Hz, plus a second up to 5K at 120Hz or 4K at 200Hz



Up to three external displays over a single Thunderbolt port


Now discontinued
From $1,699




How Much Faster Is It, Really?

The latest refresh is minor for ordinary work and significant for AI workflows. Against the M4, Apple claims 40% faster CPU performance and 2x faster graphics, which is a normal generational step, alongside unusually large gains of up to 4x faster AI performance and up to 4.8x faster prompt processing in LM Studio. Almost all of the engineering appears to have gone into AI optimization, in the form of Neural Accelerators built into every GPU core for the first time on the ‌Mac mini‌ and a Neural Engine doubled to two 16-core units. The M5 Pro follows the same pattern, at up to 4x faster than the M4 Pro for prompt processing but only 1.4x faster for ray-traced rendering in Blender.
 
Display support is the one significant change beyond the chips. Both models add 4K at 165Hz and variable refresh rate, which the 2024 machines never supported, and the M5 Pro can drive a second display at 5K at 120Hz where the M4 Pro capped it at 6K at 60Hz. If you own a high refresh rate monitor, this is perhaps the most noticeable difference in the entire update.

It is worth noting that Apple's figure of up to 170GB/s for the M6 only applies to the 24GB and 32GB configurations. The 16GB models run at 153GB/s, so the gain over the M4's 120GB/s is around 28% for many buyers rather than the 42% implied. Bandwidth governs how fast a model's weights move out of memory, which makes the 32GB configuration a faster machine.
 
The memory ceilings are also not the increases they appear to be. The M4 shipped with a 32GB option and the M4 Pro with 64GB when they launched in October 2024, and Apple removed both in May as memory prices climbed. The new models restore those ceilings rather than raising them, so a 32GB M4 or 64GB M4 Pro already has the same ceiling as its 2026 equivalent.

Which to Choose?

If you own a 2024 ‌Mac mini‌ and do not run AI models on it, skip this generation. A 40% CPU improvement is not something you will notice in daily use, and nothing else meaningful about the machine has changed. The exception is display support: if you have a high refresh rate monitor stuck at 60Hz, that is a real problem the new models solve and the old ones never will.
 
If you do run models locally, the upgrade is easy to justify from an M4, but more difficult from an M4 Pro. Roughly 4x faster prompt processing changes what you can attempt. From an M4 Pro you get unchanged GPU core counts, a 12% bandwidth increase, and a $300 rise over what you paid, so wait for the next year's revision unless you specifically need to upgrade to a 64GB model.
 
For new buyers, the gap between the two 2026 models is wider than the $800 price difference suggests: the M5 Pro has 80% more memory bandwidth, double the memory ceiling, and 50% more CPU cores at the top. Since tools like LM Studio and Ollama run on the GPU rather than the Neural Engine, capacity and bandwidth are what matter. Memory capacity decides which models you can load at all, while bandwidth determines how fast they run. If your models fit in 32GB, buy the M6 at $899. If they do not, the M5 Pro is your only option here.
 
The 2024 models remain worth considering even though Apple has stopped selling them new, with availability via third parties, Apple's refurbished store, or second-hand.
 
Do not expect prices to collapse in the usual way, whichever route you take. The memory shortage pushed Apple's prices up, twice during the M4's final year, so a modest discount off $799 is unremarkable. The M4 model is worth buying nearer the $599 it launched at, and much above that, the stretch to buy a new M6 is difficult to argue against.
 
The 32GB M4 and 64GB M4 Pro were only sold between October 2024 and May 2026, so they exist on the used market but were unavailable new for the machine's final months. A 64GB M4 Pro matches the memory ceiling of a $1,699 M5 Pro at 273GB/s against 307GB/s, for considerably less. For running larger models on a budget, that may be the most cost-effective configuration.

title: iPhone Air 2 Could Replace iPhone 18, Sketchy Rumor Claims
content:
Apple may be considering scrapping the standard iPhone 18 entirely and rebranding the iPhone Air 2 as its new $999 entry point when the more affordable iPhone models launch in spring 2027, a sketchy rumor claims.


The claim comes from the X account "Early Apple," who said Apple is "exploring the idea" of having the Air 2 simply take over the ‌iPhone 18‌ name and price point rather than launching as a separate device. 

iPhone 18 Pro models and Apple's first foldable iPhone arriving later this month. Given how firmly that three way split has held up in the rumor cycle so far, a rebrand this drastic looks unlikely for 2027.

covered leaks from the account before, including an alleged ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ prototype photo back in April, but as we noted at the time, Early Apple is a relatively new account of unknown origin with no established track record, so the claim is best treated as an informed guess. The rumor has gained some traction online, so we have covered it for the sake of completeness.

Jon Prosser raised a similar possibility months ago, suggesting Apple's ultra-thin design could eventually become the template for the standard iPhone rather than remaining a separate niche model, framing it as a longer term shift rather than something arriving as soon as next spring.

There is a reasonable case for some convergence over time, even if next year is too soon. Apple has a history of debuting design features on pricier models before trickling down to the standard iPhone in later years, and with the ‌iPhone Air‌ 2 expected to close the gap by adding a second rear camera, one of the biggest practical differences between the Air and the standard iPhone would disappear. That makes it plausible that a future standard iPhone could eventually resemble the Air, even if an outright merger during the upcoming product cycle remains a stretch.

title: Is the John Ternus honeymoon already over?
content:
Macworld





John Ternus has been Apple CEO all of a week so it’s time to start stirring things up! Hey, he’s had seven whole days!
Writing for Bloomberg, Mark Gurman is here to dish the dirt and lob some Baby Ruths over the fence and into Ternus’s pool, and he’s all out of, uh, dirt, I guess, in this metaphor? That one kind of got away from the Macalope.
“Tim Cook’s CEO-Like Pay Package Shows He Isn’t Going Anywhere” (subscription required)
In regard to the timing of Cook’s exit, Gurman says it’s to give Ternus “a massive tailwind” while Apple is at the top of its game.
If Cook waited another two or three years to give the job to Ternus, the cupboard of genuinely new and impressive products could be bare.
BREAKING: APPLE ALMOST OUT OF IDEAS. ONLY TWO OR THREE YEARS UNTIL COMPANY SHIPS VISION PRO SOCKS.
It’s also unclear where Apple would sit in the technology hierarchy after OpenAI and Anthropic become public companies…
Right where it sits now? The Macalope will just leave this piece by Horace Dediu right there for you. Pondering AI’s “killer app” moment, which has yet to happen, Dediu says:
I don’t think it’s ChatGPT. That’s like saying TCP/IP. That’s like saying Intel 8088…
Having worked first for 9to5Mac and now Bloomberg, Gurman has not seen the world from the trenches of corporate America (“IT WAS HELL,” RECALLS SURVIVOR).
It would mark a first for Apple, whose previous CEO transitions were anything but orderly, including Cook’s own succession of Jobs amid the company co-founder’s illness.
While you could point to a few things that could have gone better (Scott Forstall), the transition from Jobs to Cook was hardly a “The Purge”-style nightmare of fear, bedlam, and anarchy. It’s not like Jobs died and the Board of Directors broke a pool cue and locked Apple executives in a meeting room to fight for the position. Jobs made Cook CEO. That was pretty much that.
Again, other than Scott Forstall, whose dog apparently ate the memo.
Gurman is not wrong, however, about Cook’s new salary and position being an unusual arrangement that raises a lot of questions about just how this is all going to work. It’ll probably be fine, but it’s probably also not going to be that different, which makes one wonder how Ternus will be able to make his mark on the company.
Gurman has one more decidedly not “fun-sized” Baby Ruth to lob, this time into the Apple community’s collective pool.
But there’s a bit more to the story, I’m told.
TERNUS IS MIKE MARKKULA’S SECRET LOVE CHILD… wait, no, that’s not it.

				
					

				
			
If you’d like to receive regular news and updates to your inbox, sign up for our newsletters, including The Macalope and Apple Breakfast, David Price’s weekly, bite-sized roundup of all the latest Apple news and rumors.

Foundry





Ternus and services chief Eddy Cue want to make even more money from the App Store and figure out ways to raise margins and squeeze additional recurring revenue from the platform. Schiller, on the other hand, seems to believe that such moves will only further irk developers and governments. While there was no internal blowup or anything like that, it’s something he wanted no part of.
It would be ironic if, after years of developers dragging Schiller for App Store woes, he turned out to be the one keeping it from being even worse all along. (If this turns out to be the case, in lieu of sending Phil a nice fruit basket, developers can just send donations to the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution.)
But you have to wonder who Gurman’s sources are here. It’s not like Schiller called him and said, “Mark, it is time I told you the dark secret about the App Store! Do you have a pen? Because I’ll be naming names. First off… CUE. That’s with a ‘C,’ not a ‘Q’.” Certainly no one close to these executives spoke to Gurman. So who else would be in a position to know (or think they know) and be willing to talk out of school? Certainly a former Apple employee might be willing, which makes it possible that the sound you hear is the grinding of some axes.
No, not that sound. That sound is your CD of “Pocket Full of Kryptonite” by The Spin Doctors that fell behind the credenza in 1998 and landed in front of the air vent and has been rattling ever since. This is more of a GEEENEEERRRRRTTTT noise. Yeah, that’s the one.
Let’s just be clear that the Macalope really hopes Gurman is wrong about this. Apple has already been blinkered enough on the issue, and the idea of it doubling down and raising its take or worsening terms for developers really boggles the imagination. Maybe this represents attitudes Ternus and Cue no longer have; maybe cooler heads will still prevail.
Or maybe we’re just going to keep complaining about the App Store until the heat death of the universe.
